channel.title: Institute for Lebanon — New Documents
channel.description: Declassified U.S. State Department diplomatic cables on Lebanon's civil war and Palestinian armed presence, annotated for scholars and the public.

item.title: Three Hours That Started a War
item.description: On April 13, 1975, violence erupted in the Beirut suburb of Ain el-Rummaneh and ignited Lebanon's fifteen-year civil war. The U.S. Embassy dispatched this cable at the highest urgency level before noon the following morning. It documents three separate incidents — two of them Palestinian attacks on a Christian political gathering — before the bus massacre that history has recorded as the sole event of that day. That same evening, Palestinian forces fired rockets from a refugee camp into a Christian neighborhood. By morning, the Palestinian leadership was already framing the entire day as one-sided Christian aggression.
